solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Evidence of privileged upbringing, but one hangs by the neck

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the necktie of a public school, a badge of an elite education
second meaning, taken literally: any tie is something that hangs from the neck

explanation.surface: A grim picture of a privileged person meeting a hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangs by the neck' sounds like the gallows, but a necktie hangs there harmlessly. The old school tie also stands for the network of favours among former public schoolboys.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a symbol of an expensive private schooling and, literally, a necktie worn round the collar.

clue.text: Boy's round blemish

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a scar is a mark that spoils the skin

explanation.surface: A lad has a circular mark on his skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar is a male first name, so a boy can be called that.

clue.text: Remarkably old with active, luxurious existence

indicators.note: doing something remarkably means in an unusual way, so the letters that follow are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly person who keeps busy lives in comfort and style.
explanation.definitionFit: La dolce vita is Italian for 'the sweet life', a life of pleasure and self-indulgence.

clue.text: Barristers' memoirs, or medical records?

definitions.meaning: playful meaning: the stories of the cases a lawyer has argued
usual meaning: the documented background of a patient

explanation.surface: Wondering whether lawyers' reminiscences or doctors' notes are meant.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first reading is a whimsical one: a barrister's 'cases' with their 'histories'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors keep a case history for each patient, and a barrister's recollections would literally be histories of cases.

clue.text: Regularly poor bargain is trying experience

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word
a deal is an agreement or bargain

explanation.surface: Constantly getting bad deals is an unpleasant experience.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe test or painful experience, something trying to endure.

clue.text: Where dirty clothes may be absurdly taken for repair

indicators.note: something sent for repair is broken and has to be put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clothes are bizarrely dropped off to be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absurdly' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; the signal is 'for repair'.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundry basket is the hamper where worn clothes wait to be washed.

clue.text: Doctrine is associated with Mass

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A religious teaching linked with the Catholic Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass suggests a church service, but here it is the physics quantity, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is any distinctive theory or belief system, from the suffix of words like Marxism.

clue.text: Good health for son — just what is needed

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
S is the standard abbreviation for son
'that's it' means exactly the thing required

explanation.surface: Something healthy for a boy is exactly what he requires.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a toast used when drinking, wishing the company well, like 'cheers'.

clue.text: For hearing, disposes of body parts

indicators.note: a version for hearing is one meant for the ear, so it is the sound that counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to sell something is to dispose of it for money

explanation.surface: Someone gets rid of organs, perhaps sinister trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Cells are the tiny units the body is built from, so they are parts of it.

clue.text: Band member first to dance with stranger

indicators.note: first to means the opening letter of the next word is all that is used

parts.note: the opening letter
rum is British slang for odd, so rummer means odder

explanation.surface: A musician is the first to take to the floor with an unfamiliar person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' reads as a noun, a person you do not know; it is the comparative adjective 'more strange'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer plays percussion and is a standard part of a group of musicians.

clue.text: Port or whiskey?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., an old harbour town in East Sussex, one of the Cinque Ports
second meaning: a whiskey distilled from ... grain

explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the fortified wine, offered as an alternative drink to whiskey; here it is a harbour town in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is both a historic English coastal town and the name of an American-style grain whiskey.

clue.text: Speech introduced by His Excellency that is about the crown

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
an address is a formal speech

explanation.surface: An ambassador makes a speech about the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduced by' puts the title in front of the speech. The crown here is the top of the head, not the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A headdress is a covering or ornament worn on the head, so it sits around the top of one's skull.

clue.text: Country supports me over American issue

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the short word just before it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
A is a standard abbreviation for American
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A nation backs the speaker against an American matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like 'above', but it turns ME round. In a down clue, one piece supporting another sits beneath it, so the country comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that issues or flows out from a source, so the noun issue fits.

clue.text: Sign of spring changes, after the start

indicators.note: taking only what comes after the start means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to vary is to change

explanation.surface: Something signalling spring changes once it has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the word to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries is the zodiac sign beginning at the March equinox, the first sign of the spring season.

clue.text: Fool is trying initially to be of use

parts.note: an ass is a stupid person
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the preceding word is used

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A fool keeps trying hard to be helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help someone, which is being useful to them.

clue.text: As found in still, it helps to create alcohol

indicators.note: something found in another thing sits inside it, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: yet and still both mean up to now, even so
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something present in a distillery still helps make spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' sounds like the distilling apparatus; it is the adverb meaning 'even now'. Fermentation happens before distillation, which the surface fudges.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus that ferments sugar into alcohol in brewing and winemaking.

clue.text: No good in roughly pulling jacket

indicators.note: 'no' says the following item is absent, so it is taken out of the word

parts.note: to jerk is to pull sharply and roughly
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: It does no good to tug hard at a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a short sleeveless jacket, historically of leather.

clue.text: American in very popular period drama on TV

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the following words

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
A is a standard abbreviation for American
pop is short for popular, as in pop music
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An American features in a hit costume drama on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period drama' looks like a single unit, but period is a separate piece and drama joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama broadcast on television or radio.

clue.text: In the morning clinging to current objective

indicators.note: clinging to means wrapping around something, so the first piece hugs the second from both sides

parts.note: a.m. marks times in the morning
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Holding on to an up-to-date goal first thing in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as meaning present-day; in crosswords it is often the physics symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is a goal or target, which is what an objective is.

clue.text: Men almost knocked over slippery customer in brawl

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so in a down entry the word runs bottom to top

parts.note: an eel is a proverbially slippery creature, and slang for a shifty person

explanation.surface: Some men nearly floored a slippery character in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused hand-to-hand fight among several people.

clue.text: Suffering from queasiness induced by unsettling passage?

definitions.text: Suffering from queasiness induced by unsettling passage

parts.note: surface reading: a disturbing paragraph of text that makes one feel ill
setter's reading: a passage is a voyage across water, and a rough one upsets the stomach

explanation.surface: A reader feels nauseous after an upsetting extract.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the double reading of passage: writing, or a trip by ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea brought on by the motion of a boat on rough water is the classic form of travel sickness.

clue.text: Scottish town's atmosphere remarked on

indicators.note: something remarked on is spoken, so what counts is how the word sounds

parts.note: air is the atmosphere we breathe

explanation.surface: People comment on the ambience of a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a coastal town in south-west Scotland, home of a famous racecourse.

clue.text: Little crustaceans back finally at small brook

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the preceding word is used

parts.note: the closing letter
a rill is a tiny stream

explanation.surface: Tiny shellfish return at last to a little stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the word whose last letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are small shrimp-like crustaceans that form the main food of many whales.

clue.text: Here teens mangled form of verb

parts.note: someone here is present

indicators.note: something mangled is crushed out of shape, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Teenagers here have butchered a verb's grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here teens mangled' tempts you to anagram both words; only the teens are mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: The present tense is the verb form describing what is happening now, as in 'she walks'.
